content.title: Masters 2026: The prize money that the winner and the rest of the field will take home
content.text: SportsRory McIlroy, of Northern Ireland, reacts after winning in a playoff against Justin Rose after the final round at the Masters golf tournament, April 13, 2025, in Augusta, Ga.(AP Photo/Matt Slocum)By Brian Linder | blinder@pennlive.comThe Masters is slated to get underway today at Augusta National, and along with a chance to get into the history books, the competitors will be playing for some big-time bucks.According to reports, the prize pool for this year’s event is estimated to be “at least $21 million,” with the winner slated to take home around $4.2 million.The official prize pool will be announced on Saturday. TheGolfNewsNet.com reported that the pool was bumped up by $1 million last year, but a chunk of that — $600,000 — went into the winner’s purse. The site said that the winner of the Masters is guaranteed to take home 20 percent of the payout.Second place will take home an estimated $2,268,000, third will get an estimated $1,428,000 and fourth is slated to receive an estimated $1,008,000.Fifth place will get an estimated $840,000, sixth $756,000, seventh $703,500 and eighth $651,000.A top 20 finish plays pretty good, too.In fact, the 20th spot is slated to pay an estimated $273,000 while the 24th spot is slated to pay out $201,000.Even a top 40 finish isn’t bad money, with the 40th slot estimated to pay out $90,300.There is good news for players who make the field, but don’t fare well in Georgia this weekend, too. Per TheGolfNewsNet.com players who miss the cut will get $25,000, which is an increase of $15,000.The amateurs in the tournament will not be paid. The field is led by Rory McIlroy, Scottie Scheffler, Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau.Brian Linder is the trending editor at PennLive.com.
